headline: A Mount Sinai study found that a short safety reminder lowered, but did not eliminate, the harmful medical choices made by AI chatbots.
score_reason: Useful safety result, but the paper was published on 26 Sep 2026 and only publicised on 8 Oct; lowered by 1 from 5.
importance_line: Shows that how an AI tool is instructed changes its clinical safety, which matters to patients and hospitals adopting it, but about 1 in 10 answers were still potentially harmful and the tests were written scenarios, not real patients.
summary: Medical Economics reports that researchers at Mount Sinai's Icahn School of Medicine tested 20 large language models on more than 10 million responses and found that a brief safety reminder cut potentially harmful clinical choices from 16.6% to 10.1%, with the drop seen in 19 of the 20 models. The authors stress that harmful choices still appeared in roughly 1 in 10 responses and that a reminder is one safeguard, not a substitute for clinical oversight.
notes: Mount Sinai page blocked (edgesuite error); written from Medical Economics, which cites the Mount Sinai study published 26 Sep 2026 in Communications Medicine.
